Planted Roma tomato seeds in a bucket today; tips?

it should be in at least 5 gal bucket. 10-10-10 slow realease about a tablespoon, followed by 10-10-10 liquid every few weeks. dont over water. make sure your container has holes for drainage. it needs full sun so place where it gets the best. you may wanna check local places for blossum end rot, id suggest if you have a coffee grinder to grind eggshells and mix them in the soil maybe a 1/2 tablesppon or so.
What does the 10-10-10 mean? I'm pretty new to all of this.

The numbers refer to the nutrient content of the fertilizer...specifically Nitrogen (N), Potassium(P), and Phosphorus(K). The numbers don't matter that much. You just want to get some fertilizer that has numbers that are somewhat close to each other so you get all the nutrients. Some fertilizers are for foliage only and have a high first number...like 27,0,0. You don't want that.

If you just buy some Miracle Grow fertilizer in the square box and follow the directions and you'll be fine. It is a good choice because it has small amounts of other nutrients in addition to the N,P,K. It is also easy to apply in accurate amounts so it is great for beginners.

Water consistently to ensure the toms don't split open on the plant i.e. don't give them loads one day, nothing for 3 days, some on day 4, nothing for 2 days etc.

Ensure there is good airflow around the plant i.e. don't cram too many in together.

Use some liquid tomato feed once the fruit appear. Use as directed on the bottle.
